content: Dr. Thomas Robert Tom Mason, born on April 29, 1920, and deceased on December 1, 1980, was a chiropractor residing in Los Angeles during the 1950s. He is most notably recognized for serving as the stand-in for the recently deceased actor Bela Lugosi in Edward D. Wood Jr.'s infamous film Plan 9 From Outer Space. Dr. Mason, who was taller than Lugosi and bore only a questionable physical resemblance to him, performed his scenes hunched over with a cape held over his face to obscure the differences in appearance. Beyond this role, Dr. Mason also appeared in and contributed to the production of a few other films by Ed Wood, including Night of the Ghouls—in which he was allowed to show his face—and Final Curtain. Following these projects, his involvement in the entertainment industry came to an end. Dr. Mason passed away in 1980. In popular culture, he was portrayed by actor Ned Bellamy in the 1994 biographical film Ed Wood.
